patient_information: A 16-year-old Malawian girl, recently delivered a baby 5 months ago, with unremarkable past medical history except for a negative antenatal HIV test; lives with parents, three siblings and baby in an urban high-density area with no running water or electricity, fetching water from a community tap; dropped out of primary school during pregnancy.
chief_complaint: Fever, generalized abdominal pain, and frontal headache for 5 days.
history_of_present_illness: A 16-year-old Malawian girl presented to the emergency room with fever, generalized abdominal pain, and frontal headache for the past 5 days; she delivered a baby 5 months ago, and an antenatal HIV test was negative.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient lives with her parents, her three siblings, and her baby in an urban high-density area with no running water or electricity, fetching water from a community tap.
vitals: Temperature 38.1 0C (100.6 0F), blood pressure 110/60mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, respiratory rate 20 breath cycles per minute, Glasgow Coma Scale 15/15.
physical_exam: Mild scleral jaundice, no neck stiffness; abdomen shows diffuse tenderness but no guarding, liver not enlarged, spleen palpable at 2cm below the left costal margin; chest is clear, no lymphadenopathy; pelvic examination unremarkable with no vaginal discharge.
labs_and_diagnostics: Blood film for malaria parasites was positive with low parasitaemia; laboratory results on admission showed WBC 3.2 (x10^9/L), Haemoglobin 10.9 (mg/dL), MCV 90 (fL), Platelets 164 (x10^9/L), and Creatinine 71 ( 5mol/L); liver function tests were unavailable due to lack of reagents.
differential_diagnosis: Malaria, enteric fever (typhoid or paratyphoid), and invasive non-typhoidal salmonellae (iNTS) in HIV-positive patients.
management_and_clinical_course: On admission, patient was started on artemether/lumefantrine PO and ceftriaxone 2g IV od; a repeat HIV test was negative; blood cultures grew Salmonella Typhi; antibiotic therapy was switched to ciprofloxacin 500mg bid for 10 days; fever settled and patient felt better by day 5 of antibiotic treatment; discharged on day 7; also given one dose of praziquantel due to schistosomiasis endemicity.
